question: What will I learn in the Database subject?
answer:
In the Database subject (32606), you will learn the following:

1. Basic concepts of database design and its implementation, including relational design through entity-relationship diagrams (ERDs) and their interpretation.
2. How to use Structured Query Language (SQL) for data retrieval from databases.
3. Skills related to the coding required for database implementation.

Additionally, the subject includes practical knowledge gained through lectures and labs, where you will engage in activities such as drawing ERDs and working with SQL.

[32113 Advanced Database | Learning and teaching activities]
The subject is comprised of lectures and workshops. Students will learn advanced data management through hands-on workshops supported by online lecture and reading material. Students are expected to prepare for the lecture and workshop by studying required material in order to participate in-class activities. 

This is a project-based subject in which teams of students will develop a database system to meet customer requirements. So far as possible the customer requirements will be commercially realistic, and the project will be performed in a commercially realistic manner. Periodically students will present their work for review before presenting the finished product for evaluation.

[32606 Database | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject introduces basic concepts of database design and its implementation, including relational design through entity-relationship diagrams and their interpretation. You'll learn to use SQL for data retrieval from databases and gain skills into the coding required for database implementation.

[32606 Database | Learning and teaching activities]
There will be a two-hour lecture and one hour of tutorial. The two-hour lecture slot will not be used entirely for content delivery, it will be used as a question-answer session as well. The one-hour lab will be used for gaining practical knowledge of SQL and designing ERD. However, during the lab time, there will be two assessments conducted which are SQL test1 and SQL test2. The lectures and labs will be conducted via Zoom interactive sessions.

 Students collaborate by engaging in consultation with their peers and instructor to interpret design requirement and create entity relationship diagrams.

 Assessments are designed in such a way that the students receive almost immediate feedback for every assessment item except for the final assessment.

 Assessments 3 and 4, students will do a class tests, these assessments will test students’ ability to draw an E-R diagram from a given scenario and answer questions relating to database integrity.

 For the final assessment the database project, students will create a database of their own choosing, their choice based on a database that is currently being used in the real world.

 Please note that students are expected to put in additional study and practice time of your own in order to develop the practical skills necessary to fulfill the subject learning objectives.

 Students are expected to use Canvas as part of their learning experience for this subject. Software tools to be used is PostgreSQL, which is a database management system, and other web-based applications that offer students the opportunity to develop their SQL skills.

To learn more about requisites, please visit the How to use the Handbook guide.

Recommended pre-reading for 32606 Database

- Michael Mannino, Database Application Development.
- ISBN: 0072463678.

This text is recommended as background reading for students who want to become familiar with database concepts and database application development before or during the subject.

[32113 Advanced Database | Additional subject details]
Recommended studies

SLO3: Critically evaluate database designs and the role databases play in effective software applications. (C.1)

- Due: 4 September 2026 at 14:00

Assessment 2: SQL Test 2
- Due: 11 September 2026 at 14:00
- Weight/points shown in Canvas: 20 points

Assessment 3: ACID Properties and Integrity Constraints
- Due: 15 September 2026 at 11:11
- Weight/points shown in Canvas: 20 points
- Short written responses on entity, domain and referential integrity, ACID properties, and an ERD task based on a supplied scenario.

Assessment 4: ERD Task
- Due: 29 September 2026 at 11:11
- Weight/points shown in Canvas: 20 points
- Students draw an entity-relationship diagram from a supplied database scenario and identify the required relationships accurately.

Assessment 5: Database Project
- Due: 5 October 2026 at 23:59
- Weight/points shown in Canvas: 20 points
- Students design and build a small database project based on a self-selected real-world problem, develop an ERD, and obtain feedback on the proposed design.

[32601 Advanced Project Management | Learning and teaching activities]
This subject is taught through a one hour lecture and two hour tutorial each week on the City campus. The lectures and tutorials are structured to reflect how projects operate in the real world—blending theory, discussion, and scenario testing into one continuous and interactive learning session. 

Each week, you’ll explore key concepts in advanced project management, including leadership, ethics, stakeholder engagement, governance, and delivery frameworks. These ideas won’t just be discussed in theory—they’ll be applied immediately through realistic project scenarios, ethical dilemmas, or stakeholder challenges. You'll be encouraged to test your assumptions, make decisions, and reflect on the outcomes in real time. 

Workshops are highly collaborative and designed to simulate the workplace. You’ll work in project teams across the semester to respond to briefs, engage with case studies, and co-develop a group tender submission. These teams are expected to manage their own work through tools such as Kanban boards, team roles, and meeting notes—just as you would in industry. 

You’ll also complete individual reflections where you critically evaluate your leadership style, emotional intelligence, and decision-making. It is critical for assessment purposes these reflections are grounded in evidence from your team experience and supported by theory introduced in class. 

This subject integrates thinking and doing throughout. Participation, initiative, and reflection are essential—for both learning current practice, and for enhancing the skills expected of a professional advanced project manager.

[32601 Advanced Project Management | Additional subject details]
Professional standards
Students enrolled in the Master of Professional Engineering should note that this subject contributes to the development of the following Engineers Australia Stage 1 competencies: 

- 1.4 Discernment of knowledge development and research directions within the engineering discipline. 

- 2.4 Application of systematic approaches to the conduct and management of engineering projects.

- 3.1 Ethical conduct and professional accountability.

- 3.4 Professional use and management of information

- 3.5 Orderly management of self and professional conduct.

Recommended studies
It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge have prior knowledge of project management principles and some level of relevant practical experience

[32601 Advanced Project Management | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject is focused on the so-called “soft” aspects of Project management. In this subject, you'll grasp the intricacies of project management within a global business context, focusing on human and organisational dynamics, project governance, and the evolving role of project managers. You'll develop critical skills in teamwork, analysis, and research, enabling you to tackle complex business solutions effectively. Learning is interactive and collaborative, featuring in-class flipped learning sessions, discussions, and group projects that encourage critical thinking. You'll also undertake individual research, formulating and defending your own perspectives on relevant issues.

question: What does Fundamentals of Software Development officially cover, and what will I actually study in the Week 1 module?
answer:
The "Fundamentals of Software Development" subject officially covers a foundation in modern software development, including both theoretical and practical aspects of software modeling and development methods, tools, and techniques. You will learn how to analyze, design, develop, and evaluate software programs that implement realistic but manageably small-scale software requirements.

In the Week 1 module, you will study the following topics:

[32601 Advanced Project Management | Learning and teaching activities]
This subject is taught through a one hour lecture and two hour tutorial each week on the City campus. The lectures and tutorials are structured to reflect how projects operate in the real world—blending theory, discussion, and scenario testing into one continuous and interactive learning session. 

Each week, you’ll explore key concepts in advanced project management, including leadership, ethics, stakeholder engagement, governance, and delivery frameworks. These ideas won’t just be discussed in theory—they’ll be applied immediately through realistic project scenarios, ethical dilemmas, or stakeholder challenges. You'll be encouraged to test your assumptions, make decisions, and reflect on the outcomes in real time. 

Workshops are highly collaborative and designed to simulate the workplace. You’ll work in project teams across the semester to respond to briefs, engage with case studies, and co-develop a group tender submission. These teams are expected to manage their own work through tools such as Kanban boards, team roles, and meeting notes—just as you would in industry. 

You’ll also complete individual reflections where you critically evaluate your leadership style, emotional intelligence, and decision-making. It is critical for assessment purposes these reflections are grounded in evidence from your team experience and supported by theory introduced in class. 

This subject integrates thinking and doing throughout. Participation, initiative, and reflection are essential—for both learning current practice, and for enhancing the skills expected of a professional advanced project manager.

[32113 Advanced Database | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

Software systems require trustworthy data management systems. This subject covers advanced database concepts, requirements, architecture, design and systems. Current trends and challenges in the practice of data management are explored to develop the robust data solutions. In small teams, students apply these contemporary data management practices to their advanced database project work. Students learn to integrate and manage data from different sources to support the data-intensive software systems.

[32606 Database | Learning and teaching activities]
There will be a two-hour lecture and one hour of tutorial. The two-hour lecture slot will not be used entirely for content delivery, it will be used as a question-answer session as well. The one-hour lab will be used for gaining practical knowledge of SQL and designing ERD. However, during the lab time, there will be two assessments conducted which are SQL test1 and SQL test2. The lectures and labs will be conducted via Zoom interactive sessions.

 Students collaborate by engaging in consultation with their peers and instructor to interpret design requirement and create entity relationship diagrams.

 Assessments are designed in such a way that the students receive almost immediate feedback for every assessment item except for the final assessment.

 Assessments 3 and 4, students will do a class tests, these assessments will test students’ ability to draw an E-R diagram from a given scenario and answer questions relating to database integrity.

 For the final assessment the database project, students will create a database of their own choosing, their choice based on a database that is currently being used in the real world.

 Please note that students are expected to put in additional study and practice time of your own in order to develop the practical skills necessary to fulfill the subject learning objectives.

 Students are expected to use Canvas as part of their learning experience for this subject. Software tools to be used is PostgreSQL, which is a database management system, and other web-based applications that offer students the opportunity to develop their SQL skills.

[32113 Advanced Database | Learning and teaching activities]
The subject is comprised of lectures and workshops. Students will learn advanced data management through hands-on workshops supported by online lecture and reading material. Students are expected to prepare for the lecture and workshop by studying required material in order to participate in-class activities. 

This is a project-based subject in which teams of students will develop a database system to meet customer requirements. So far as possible the customer requirements will be commercially realistic, and the project will be performed in a commercially realistic manner. Periodically students will present their work for review before presenting the finished product for evaluation.

- Short written responses on entity, domain and referential integrity, ACID properties, and an ERD task based on a supplied scenario.

Assessment 5: Database Project
